title: Creamy Chorizo Pasta
subtitle: One pot · ready in 20 minutes
description: A smoky, garlicky one-pot pasta where the shapes cook straight in the stock and soak up all the chorizo flavour. A spoonful of balsamic at the end cuts through the cream.

steps.text: Warm a drizzle of olive oil in a deep skillet over medium heat. Add the onion and garlic and fry until softened.
Add the chorizo and fry until it releases its oil. For a richer sauce, stir in a tablespoon of tomato paste here.

Stir in the paprika and oregano, then add about 500ml of the stock and the pasta — just enough to cover it. Lid on and simmer until nearly al dente, stirring now and then and topping up with stock if it starts to stick.
Lid off. Pour in the cream and balsamic, season with salt and pepper, and stir. Simmer to thicken the sauce and finish cooking the pasta.
When it's as saucy as you like and the pasta is al dente, divide between bowls and top with grated parmesan and chives.

notes: Use good Spanish cooking chorizo (the firm, cured kind) and cube it yourself rather than buying thin slices.
Roughly 100g of dried pasta per person is a good portion guide.
Leftovers keep 2–3 days in the fridge; reheat gently with a splash of milk or water to loosen the sauce.
